history.dynasty: Koch kingdom (Naranarayan era); land grants from Ahom kings
history.period: Established end of 1549 AD (1468 Saka) by Srimanta Sankardev
history.summary: Patbaushi Satra — 'Sankardev's Thaan' — was established by Srimanta Sankardev at the end of 1549 AD (1468 Saka) at Patbaushi (also called Baushi Bilayat / Baraljar), near Barpeta in the Koch kingdom, after he fled the Ahom kingdom; he built a Kirtanghar here. It lies about 5 km southeast of Barpeta town (CSV town 'Barpeta' is approximate). One cultural source says the Guru spent about 18 years here and completed the Kirtan Ghosa (flagged as tradition, not hard evidence). Damodardev was initiated by Sankardev here and given a sattra of his own at Patbaushi; he later founded the Brahma Sanghati sect. Koch king Raghudeva presented the satra a brass Chandi statue, and Ahom kings donated 64 bighas of land. Preserved relics include Sankardeva's paduka (wooden footwear), a 12-inch pira used by Madhabdeva, wooden masks and statues, Sanchipat puthis written by both saints, the Aai Goshanir Patkuwa (ring well) built for Kalindi Aai, and the Rangiyal flower garden; Ram Ata instituted the padadhuli (foot-dust) custom here. There is currently no Satradhikar, and women are not permitted inside the Kirtanghar per satra rule. Coordinates are a full-address geocode match for the satra.

name: Patbaushi Satra
town_description: Barpeta is the headquarters town of Barpeta district in Lower Assam, about 95-130 km northwest of Guwahati. Known as the 'Satra Nagari' (town of satras), it grew around Madhavdeva's Barpeta Satra and its twenty-two hatis, and remains the historic centre of the Ekasarana Vaishnavite tradition, with handloom weaving and bell-metal work as local crafts.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati (approx. 95-130 km; ~2.5-3 hours by road).
travel.railway: Barpeta Road (Simlaguri) station, approx. 13-14 km from Barpeta town.
travel.road: The satra is about 5 km southeast of Barpeta town on the Dhanukhanda jaan side; reached by auto/taxi from Barpeta town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Deul/Doul festival season (February-March) for the main festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily for prayer and kirtan; a cultural school trains students in Satriya dance and bargeet on Fridays. The exact daily schedule is not published online — verify locally before travel.
